findings.location: lines 7, 16-20, and 23; related plan.md lines 31 and 157-175
findings.affected_requirement: Story 13.1 bounded capture behavior; plan.md deployment-overridable capture limits; AD-30 and AD-32 portable configured resource bounds; PRD NFR-1.1 and NFR-4.1
findings.evidence: The trust-boundary text says ordinary callers supply only Repository/ref/revision and Repository-relative read arguments, but the conceptual public AcquireAsync signature also accepts SourceCaptureLimits. The contract says the facade supplies the subject and purpose but never says it derives, clamps, or validates capture limits against deployment configuration. This leaves task generation free to expose caller-selected capture limits that bypass the mandatory configured entry, blob, aggregate, and deadline bounds, contradicting the plan's fail-closed configuration model and creating an unbounded resource-consumption seam.
findings.correction_outcome: Revise the plan set so the callable capture boundary has one deterministic limit owner: remove SourceCaptureLimits from caller input and derive it from validated deployment configuration, or define a caller request that may only lower server bounds and specify atomic validation/clamping before Git or storage work. Align the application contract, plan configuration table, failure outcomes, and planned tests so callers cannot raise capture work or deadline limits.

summary: REVISE. The pinned boundary and every listed artifact hash match the review packet, and the proposed source ownership, raw-Git capture, atomic row-visible publication, live authorization, scoped reads, recovery, compatibility, PostgreSQL qualification, and true separate-process evidence strategy otherwise fit the accepted Story 13.1 and repository architecture. The plan correctly declares both its architecture-decision trigger and the material Scan-strategy planned-change trigger. Before plan acceptance and user authorization, the capture contract must close its contradictory caller-controlled limit seam so deployment bounds remain authoritative and fail closed.
